Devonport — Plymouth, United Kingdom

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Devon & Cornwall Police recorded 870 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 17.8 per 1,000 residents, the 2nd highest rate of Plymouth's 20 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (75), drugs (5), burglary (4); the evening/night score by violent crime (91), anti social behaviour (40), public order (20). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Devonport safe?

Wandroz currently rates Devonport in Plymouth as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Plymouth, both by day and after dark. This rating is derived from Devon & Cornwall Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Devonport safe at night?

At night, Devonport is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Plymouth. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Devonport a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Devonport's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Plymouth) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

Is there official crime data for Devonport?

Yes. Devonport's rating is derived from Devon & Cornwall Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk, not an assessment — see the note on this page for the exact figure and the methodology page for full sourcing.
